stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Folklorists have long observed that animal tricksters fill several distinct roles in West African oral storytelling. Some tricksters act as fools whose schemes collapse on them, while others serve as cultural heroes. ______ the spider Anansi often appears as a bringer of knowledge: in many tellings, he wins all the world's stories from the sky god and carries them down to people on earth.
explanation: The first sentences name a category with a plural noun: 'several distinct roles.' The sentence after the blank agrees with that claim and gives one member of the category, Anansi as a bringer of knowledge. One instance drawn from a larger group takes 'For example.'

A.why: You read the narrower sentence as a restatement. 'In other words' would mean the Anansi sentence repeats the claim about several roles in different terms. Instead, it adds new information: one specific trickster and one specific role.

C.why: You took the vivid detail about the sky god as a reversal. The Anansi sentence supports the claim that tricksters serve as cultural heroes and contradicts nothing, so a contrast word does not fit.

D.why: You treated the passage as a sequence of steps or a list reaching its last item. Nothing here is ordered in time, and the sentence gives an example instead of concluding a series.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: For years, astronomers at a small mountaintop observatory struggled to capture clear images of faint, distant galaxies. In 2019, the observatory's staff made one upgrade to its main telescope that sharply improved those images. ______ they replaced the telescope's aging camera sensor with a new one able to detect nearly twice as much of the incoming light.
explanation: The second sentence mentions a single, unnamed action: 'one upgrade.' The sentence after the blank tells you exactly what that upgrade was. Nothing is being picked from a set. The same claim is being spelled out more precisely, so 'Specifically' is correct.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. You saw a general claim followed by a detail and chose 'For example.' The passage says the staff made only one upgrade, so the sensor replacement is not one example among several. It is the upgrade itself, described in detail.

B.why: You treated the detail as a contradiction. Replacing the sensor is the upgrade that improved the images, so the sentence agrees with what came before and does not push against it.

D.why: 'Similarly' introduces a second, comparable thing. The sensor replacement is not a separate change resembling the upgrade. It is the same upgrade, named.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: A 2021 study that followed 300 recreational runners through a full training season identified several habits that predicted injury. The researchers tracked each runner's mileage, footwear, sleep, and warm-up routine from week to week. ______ runners who raised their weekly distance by more than 30 percent at any point were nearly three times as likely as other runners to develop shin pain.
explanation: The passage names a category with a plural noun: 'several habits that predicted injury.' The sentence after the blank presents one of those habits, increasing mileage too fast, along with its effect. One member drawn from a larger group takes 'For instance.'

B.why: You treated the narrower sentence as a rephrasing. The mileage finding adds new information the earlier sentences never stated, such as the 30 percent threshold and the tripled risk of shin pain, so it is not a restatement.

C.why: 'Instead' signals that one option replaces another. The mileage finding doesn't replace anything. It is one of the habits the study identified.

D.why: You read the passage as a timeline. The final sentence reports a result of the study and isn't an event that came after the tracking, so a time-order word misstates the relationship.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Nutrition researchers have found that dietary fiber benefits the body in several distinct ways. ______ soluble fiber, found in oats and beans, absorbs water in the gut and forms a thick gel that slows how quickly sugar enters the bloodstream. Other kinds of fiber add bulk that helps food move steadily through the intestines.
explanation: The first sentence makes a broad claim about a group: 'several distinct ways' that fiber helps. The next sentence agrees with it and describes one of those ways, soluble fiber slowing sugar absorption. The last sentence confirms that there are others. When a sentence picks one member out of a larger set, the right transition is 'For example.'

B.why: You treated the second sentence as a reversal. It doesn't contradict the claim that fiber helps. It shows one way that fiber helps, so a contrast word doesn't fit.

C.why: You read the second sentence as a rewording of the first. It actually adds new, narrower information about one type of fiber and one effect, so it isn't the same claim in different words. This is the subtype's reverse trap.

D.why: You assumed the sentences describe steps in time. Nothing happens after anything else here. The second sentence is an instance of the first.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Materials scientists at a university laboratory recently made a single change to a ceramic commonly used in turbine parts. ______ they coated the ceramic's surface with a thin layer of zirconium oxide. The coated ceramic withstood temperatures roughly 200 degrees higher than the original before it began to crack.
explanation: The first sentence mentions one vague action: the scientists made 'a single change.' The blank sentence says exactly what that change was, a zirconium oxide coating. Nothing is being chosen from a set. The same action is just described more precisely, so 'Specifically' is the right transition.

B.why: This is the subtype's trap. 'For example' would mean the coating is one of several changes, but the passage says the scientists made a single change. The second sentence spells out that one change, so it is not a sample from a group.

C.why: You heard a contrast that isn't there. The coating doesn't go against the idea that the scientists changed the ceramic. It is the change.

D.why: 'Similarly' introduces a second, parallel case. The coating isn't a separate case that resembles the change. It is the change itself, given in detail.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Engineers who design bridges in earthquake zones rely on a variety of techniques to keep the structures standing during strong shaking. ______ many newer bridges rest on rubber-and-steel bearings that let the deck shift slightly as the ground moves beneath it. Others use heavy dampers that absorb the energy of each tremor.
explanation: The first sentence names a category, 'a variety of techniques.' The blank sentence gives one of them, flexible bearings, and the next sentence ('Others use...') shows that this technique is only one of several. A single member taken from a larger group calls for 'For example.'

B.why: 'Specifically' would mean the bearings sentence spells out the whole claim exactly. It doesn't: the passage goes on to name dampers as another technique. The bearings are one sample, not the full category stated more precisely.

C.why: You read the bearings as an effect of the first sentence. Engineers using many techniques doesn't cause bearings to exist. The bearings are one of those techniques.

D.why: 'Finally' marks the last item in a sequence. This is the first technique the passage names, and another one follows, so it is not the last step of anything.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In the decade after gray wolves returned to a remote river valley, ecologists observed one striking shift in the valley's beaver population. ______ the number of active beaver colonies along the river rose from two to eleven. The researchers think that wolves kept elk from overgrazing the willows that beavers depend on for food and building material.
explanation: The first sentence mentions 'one striking shift' but doesn't say what it was. The blank sentence tells you exactly: colonies rose from two to eleven. Because the second sentence spells out that single shift instead of picking one from several, 'Specifically' is correct.

B.why: This is the subtype's trap. The passage names one shift, so there is no group for an example to come from. The rise in colonies is that shift described in detail, not one instance among many.

C.why: 'Still' signals that something holds true despite what came before. The rise in colonies doesn't push against the first sentence. It explains what the shift was.

D.why: 'Meanwhile' points to something separate happening at the same time. The rise in colonies isn't a separate event running alongside the shift. It is the shift.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Over several centuries of trade and travel, English absorbed many words from languages spoken far from Britain. ______ the word "ketchup" most likely comes from a term in Hokkien, a language of southern China, for a sauce made from fermented fish. "Shampoo," "pajamas," and "tycoon" arrived through similar routes.
explanation: The first sentence makes a claim about a plural: 'many words' borrowed from distant languages. The blank sentence looks at one of those words, 'ketchup,' and the last sentence lists more. One member chosen from a larger set calls for 'For example.'

B.why: You treated the history of 'ketchup' as an exception. It is actually a case of the borrowing the first sentence describes, so it agrees with that sentence and doesn't contrast with it.

C.why: 'Thus' introduces a conclusion that follows from the sentence before. The origin of 'ketchup' isn't caused by or inferred from the general claim. It is an instance of that claim.

D.why: This is the subtype's reverse trap. 'In other words' means the same idea is being restated. The second sentence adds new, narrower information about one specific word, so it isn't a restatement of the first.
